item.title: Active Release-Style Calf Technique
clinicalUse: Calf stiffness/pain as adjunct to dorsiflexion/loading
patientPosition: Prone or supine with ankle free to move.
contact: Tolerable contact over gastrocnemius/soleus muscle belly, away from popliteal fossa.
forceDirection: Maintain contact while patient actively dorsiflexes/extends knee as appropriate to lengthen target tissue.
item.visualCue: Calf contact + active dorsiflexion/lengthening → re-test dorsiflexion.

subTechniques.name: Gastrocnemius–soleus — Active Soft-Tissue Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Improve pain, movement tolerance or tissue-related function when this target is clinically relevant.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supine, long sitting, prone or weight-bearing depending on the technique.
subTechniques.contact: Tolerable contact over Gastrocnemius–soleus while the tissue begins in a shortened position.
subTechniques.direction: Maintain controlled contact while the patient actively lengthens/moves the target tissue.
subTechniques.dosage: Often 3–8 slow repetitions followed by reassessment.
subTechniques.reassess: Re-test the region's original pain, range or functional task.
